problem_statement: AF_PACKET (NET_AF_PACKET) sockets cannot retrieve SO_TIMESTAMPING hardware RX timestamps via recvmsg(). A packet socket that has enabled SO_TIMESTAMPING with ZSOCK_SOF_TIMESTAMPING_RX_HARDWARE should, when receiving a packet via zsock_recvmsg(), get a control message (cmsg_level ZSOCK_SOL_SOCKET, cmsg_type ZSOCK_SO_TIMESTAMPING) carrying the net_ptp_time of the packet, with msg_controllen reflecting the aligned cmsg space (NET_CMSG_SPACE(sizeof(struct net_ptp_time))). When the caller's control buffer is too small to hold the timestamp control message, recvmsg() must instead set ZSOCK_MSG_CTRUNC, return msg_controllen 0 and no usable cmsg. Before the change AF_PACKET had no recvmsg()/cmsg support, so these timestamp control messages were never produced.

verification.reason: The problem statement is too narrow and the hidden tests enforce private/internal PTP implementation details and unrelated features, so the task cannot be made fair by adding only public interface information without dictating implementation.

problems.detail: The statement only describes AF_PACKET/NET_AF_PACKET recvmsg timestamping, but the hidden tests also check many PTP stack behaviors: BMCA comparator, PTP state machines, clock decision, foreign master handling, message post-receive timestamp fallback, transport retry, and net_if timestamp callback registration/unregistration.

Several hidden tests include implementation source files and rely on implementation-specific internal state/macros such as ptp_clk.pollfd_valid, ptp_clk.state_decision_event, PTP_L2_RECVMSG_RETRY_MS, port.l2_try_recvmsg, port.l2_recvmsg_retry_at, and msg.rx_timestamp_valid; requiring these would dictate internal implementation rather than public behavior.

The tests check many exact behaviors and values not mentioned in the statement, including eventfd wake-once semantics, PTP state-to-event mappings, clock decision dataset updates, UTC offset forcing, comparator tie-break rules, foreign master threshold/cleanup rules, and transport retry timing.
